# War Scroll Column 17 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in War Scroll Column 17 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 17:1 — "lot" vs. "lot" vs. "battle" for Hebrew goral

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "In the seventh lot" | Literal rendering of goral — lot, allotment |
| LOGOS | "In the seventh lot" | Standard DSS translation preserving the theological term |
| PNEUMA | "In the seventh battle" | Dynamic equivalent clarifying for modern readers that this means the seventh engagement |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "lot" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew goral carries theological weight as a divine allotment or dispensation, not merely a "battle." The War Scroll's use of goral is deliberate — each engagement is understood as a divinely ordained lot.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 17:1 — "subdue" vs. "subdue" vs. "overpower"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall subdue" | Standard rendering of the Hebrew verb |
| LOGOS | "shall subdue" | Formal equivalent preserving the register |
| PNEUMA | "will overpower" | More forceful dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "subdue" (EMET/LOGOS). "Subdue" accurately conveys bringing under control; "overpower" is stronger than the Hebrew warrants and loses the nuance of subjugation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 17:4 — "Sons of Light" vs. "Sons of Light" vs. "Children of Light"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Sons-of-Light" | Literal with hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "Sons of Light" | Standard DSS designation, capitalized |
| PNEUMA | "Children of Light" | Natural English; echoes NT usage |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Sons of Light" (LOGOS). Per project convention established in earlier columns, these are technical Qumran self-designations rendered with "Sons" (not "Children") and capitalized.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Project convention.

---

## 17:7 — "bring low" vs. "bring low" vs. "crush"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to bring-low" | Literal Hiphil rendering |
| LOGOS | "to bring low" | Standard formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "to crush" | Intensified dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "bring low" (LOGOS). The Hebrew verb means to humble or bring low, not to crush/destroy. PNEUMA's rendering imports violence beyond the semantic range. The same verb recurs in 17:13-14 and should be rendered consistently.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:8 — "might of the angel" vs. "power of the angel" vs. "angelic power"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "through the might-of-the-angel" | Literal construct chain |
| LOGOS | "through the power of the angel" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "through angelic power" | Restructured for natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "through the power of the angel." This preserves the Hebrew structure identifying a specific angel (Michael, named in the next clause). PNEUMA's "angelic power" generalizes what the text particularizes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:8 — "made glorious" vs. "magnified" vs. "exalted"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "He has made-glorious" | Literal Hiphil of k-b-d or g-d-l |
| LOGOS | "He has magnified" | Formal biblical register |
| PNEUMA | "He has exalted" | Dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "magnified." This captures the Hiphil sense of making great/important. EMET's "made glorious" is slightly paraphrastic; PNEUMA's "exalted" is used for a different Hebrew root (r-w-m) in 17:9.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:10 — "gods" vs. "divine beings" vs. "heavenly beings"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the gods" | Literal rendering of elim |
| LOGOS | "the divine beings" | Standard scholarly rendering avoiding polytheistic implication |
| PNEUMA | "the heavenly beings" | Accessible paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "divine beings." The Hebrew elim in Qumran literature refers to angelic/heavenly entities. EMET's "gods" is technically literal but misleading in English; PNEUMA's "heavenly beings" loses the specifically divine quality the text attributes to them.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:13 — "mystery of His deeds" vs. "mystery of His works" vs. "secret of His plans"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the mystery-of-His-deeds" | Literal construct: raz ma'asav |
| LOGOS | "the mystery of His works" | Formal rendering; "works" standard for ma'asim |
| PNEUMA | "the secret of His plans" | Dynamic; "plans" interprets ma'asim as future intent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "the mystery of His works." "Mystery" is the standard rendering of raz in the project. "Works" (ma'asim) is accurate — these are God's deeds/acts, not plans (PNEUMA imports a forward-looking sense not in the Hebrew).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
